references.text: Moses settled with Jethro and married his daughter Zipporah. Here, the father-in-law is introduced as the one Moses now takes leave of.
Jethro is called 'Reuel' here and described as a priest in Midian. Moses tended his flocks when he received his calling at the burning bush.
Jethro is mentioned again later when he hears about all that God has done for Moses and Israel, and brings Zipporah back to Moses.
Moses asks Hobab, son of Reuel, to join them. The expression 'go in peace' (לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם) shows a blessing at parting.
Eli uses the same expression 'go in peace' (לְכִי לְשָׁלוֹם) to Hannah, showing a common Hebrew farewell blessing.
Jonathan says to David 'go in peace' (לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם), the same blessing formula that Jethro uses with Moses.
The expression 'go in peace' is used again, this time by Absalom to King David.
Jacob is told to go to Egypt to see his relatives, parallel to Moses' wish to see if his brothers are still alive.
Both verses illustrate the mutual respect and blessing ('go in peace') at partings between Moses and Jethro.
